traits: Pear-shaped, whitish body: a ball up to 6 cm wide on a sterile conical stem that makes up two thirds of the height
Surface covered in small spines and large conical warts that fall off gradually, leaving small round scars
Pure white, even, soft inside when young; yellowish, then olive-brown and powdery with age
When ripe, a round pore opens at the top to release the brown spores
Under conifers and in mixed woods, alone or in groups · summer and autumn
safetyNote: Only when young, with pure white, even, soft flesh inside. Cut it in two lengthwise: a mushroom already formed inside gives away an amanita egg, which is deadly. Amanita eggs usually have no spines or warts. Spores breathed in can badly irritate the lungs.

sources.title: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Mykologie (DGfM), Fachausschuss Pilzverwertung und Toxikologie (2026). Positivliste der Speisepilze, Stand 1. Mai 2026.
